item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 301732
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Lowell, located well
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
A tropical wave with disorganized showers and thunderstorms, is
located well to the south of southwestern Mexico. This system is
expected to continue to move west-northwestward to northwestward at
10 to 15 mph. Environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual
development of this system, and a tropical depression is likely to
form during the early to middle part of next week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands in the next couple of days. Some gradual
development is possible thereafter while it moves slowly westward
across the central Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

item.title: Hurricane Karina Public Advisory Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026 
585 
WTPZ31 KNHC 302049
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Karina Advisory Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
200 PM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026
 
...KARINA GAINING STRENGTH AND MOVING OVER THE PACIFIC OCEAN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.2N 123.2W
ABOUT 950 MI...1525 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...978 MB...28.88 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was located
near latitude 17.2 North, longitude 123.2 West. Karina is moving
toward the west near 9 mph (15 km/h). A slower westward to
west-northwestward motion is expected during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher
gusts. Steady to rapid strengthening seems likely, and Karina is
forecast to become a major hurricane in a day or so.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 5 miles (10 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles
(110 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 978 mb (28.88 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Karina will affect portions of the coast
of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next
couple of days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening
surf and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your
local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026 
835 
WTPZ41 KNHC 302050
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
200 PM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026
 
Convection has become better organized around the eye of Karina 
during the past several hours, with infrared satellite imagery 
indicating the development of a cold ring of cloud tops. The most 
recent TAFB Dvorak intensity estimate remains T4.0/65 kt. However, 
the most recent objective satellite estimates are in the range of 
70-99 kt. Based on the given data, the initial intensity has been 
set to 80 kt.
 
The cyclone continues to show that the inner core structure is 
improving, and with a favorable environment, Karina should be 
strengthening for the next couple of days. During this time, Karina 
could reach major hurricane status. However, the environmental 
conditions will start to become less favorable later on Monday and 
into Tuesday, when the intensification process should come to a 
halt. As the environment becomes more hostile, due to the 
progressively cooler waters and drier air, the hurricane should 
start to weaken during the middle and latter parts of the week. The 
current NHC intensity forecast is on the higher end of the guidance, 
but is very close to HCCA.
 
The hurricane is moving westward at about 8 kt. The high pressure 
system to the north of Karina is expected to weaken due to an 
amplifying trough over the western U.S. However, there should be 
enough ridging to keep Karina on a westward to west-northwestward 
course. There is still a good amount of spread in the track models 
days 3 and beyond at this time, so there is a higher degree of 
uncertainty in how far north the cyclone will move. The latest NHC 
track forecast is a bit farther south of the previous track, but 
still follows HCCA and GDMI aids.
